subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw support a persistent plain-text TUI accessibility mode, and if so should it be a documented `ui.accessibility.plainText` preference with a defined ASCII vocabulary rather than an ad hoc set of component-specific substitutions?
rationale: This is a new user-facing configuration and presentation contract, not a repair of an already-defined behavior; the closed proposal did not establish the intended permanent API or scope.

options.title: Approve one persistent plain-text contract
options.body: Add a default-off documented preference, define consistent OpenClaw-owned ASCII alternatives, and state the pi-tui upstream boundary explicitly.

options.title: Provide a TUI-local setting instead
options.body: Avoid expanding persistent file configuration if maintainers prefer a discoverable in-product accessibility control with equivalent startup wiring.

options.title: Defer pending broader accessibility design
options.body: Keep this issue open without implementation until the TUI accessibility direction and upstream dependency strategy are set.

recommendation.title: Approve one persistent plain-text contract
recommendation.body: Add a default-off documented preference, define consistent OpenClaw-owned ASCII alternatives, and state the pi-tui upstream boundary explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history connects this person most directly to both the TUI and centralized tool-display/config surfaces affected by the contract choice.
